old_reference: For New Business Permit Pre-Assessment, applicants must submit: 1) Duly filled-out Unified Application Form (1 original); 2) Sketch / Google Map of business location with pictures of premises (1 original); 3) Notarized Certified List of Employees or Certification of No Employee (1 original); 4) Valid DTI Registration for Sole Proprietorship, SEC Registration/Articles of Incorporation for Corporation/Partnership, or CDA Registration for Cooperatives (1 photocopy); and 5) Contract of Lease with Lessor's proof of ownership if rented, or proof of ownership if owned (1 photocopy). Applications can be filed online at appbts.davaocity.gov.ph or onsite.
new_reference:
For NEW business permit pre-assessment, the charter lists the following requirements. Apply the ownership, representation, vehicle and activity conditions stated in each row. Source: Business Bureau printed pages 41-42 (PDF pages 2-3). These transcribed rows include their Where to Secure entries.

1. Duly filled-out Unified Application Form (1 original) Business Bureau or at the Web site https://busbureau.davaocity.gov.ph/ or apply online at https://appbts.davaocity.gov.ph/
2. Sketch / Google map of Business location (1 original) with pictures of the premise location Applicant
3. Certified List of Employees / Certification of no Employee (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. Valid DTI Registration for Single Proprietorship (1 photocopy) Department of Trade and Industry
5. SEC Registration, Articles of Incorporation for Partnership and Corporation (1 photocopy) Securities and Exchange Commission
6. Certificate of Cooperation, Articles of Cooperation for Cooperative (1 photocopy). Cooperative Development Authority
7. DOLE / POEA Certificate of Registration, if applicable. Department of Labor and Employment
8. DHSUD Certificate of Registration, if applicable. Department of Human Settlement and Urban Development
9. Special Power of Attorney (1 current and original) for represented – Sole Proprietorship Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
10. Partnership Resolution (1 current and original) for represented – Partnership Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
11. Secretary’s Certificate or Board Resolution for other form of ownership (1 current and original) - Corporation and Cooperative Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
12. Valid I.D. of representatives, owners (Sole Proprietor, OPC, Partnership), and Corporate Secretary (Corporation, Cooperative) - 1 photocopy each) Applicant
13. Contract of Lease and copy of the Proof of ownership by the Lessor if business location is not owned and is rented by the applicant (1 photocopy) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
14. Any proof of ownership if Business location is owned Applicant
15. consent and copy of any proof of ownership if business location is not owned and is freely used by the applicant (1 photocopy) Applicant
16. OR/CR of vehicle, if with delivery vehicle (1 photocopy each vehicle) Applicant
17. Consent for use of the vehicle if not owned by the applicant. Applicant
18. FSIC for Occupancy Permit valid in the last 9 months Bureau of Fire Protection
19. Affidavit of Undertaking that there had been no substantial changes made on the building Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
20. Other Requirements depending on the Business Activity declared Concerned Agency

old_reference: To amend a business permit due to a Change of Business Address, the applicant must provide: 1) Current Original Mayor's Permit or Application for Renewal (or Certified True Copy with Affidavit of Loss); 2) Notarized Application Affidavit of Change of Business Address; 3) Notarized SPA (Sole Proprietorship), Partnership Resolution, or Secretary's Certificate (Corporation); 4) Valid ID of representative; 5) Sketch / Google map of new location with pictures; 6) Tax Declaration or proof of ownership and Lease Contract if rented; 7) Valid FSIC for Occupancy Permit within last 9 months; and 8) Notarized Affidavit of Undertaking of no substantial building changes. A service fee of PHP 50.00 is charged at the CTO.
new_reference:
For Amendment of Business Permit - Change of Business Address, the charter lists the following requirements (printed pages 42-43; PDF pages 3-4). Preserve the stated business-form and representation conditions. Each row below includes its Where to Secure entry.

1. Current Original Mayor’s Permit, Application for Renewal of Business Permit, or Certified True Copy of Business Permit w/ Affidavit of Loss in case of lost permits Applicant or Records Section, Business Bureau or Any Notary Public for affidavit of loss.
2. Application Affidavit of Change of Business Address (notarized) stating the new location of the business-Single Proprietorship Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. For Sole Proprietorship, if represented, Special Power of Attorney, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. For Partnership, Partnership Resolution indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative, and stating the new location of the business Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. For Corporation / Cooperative, Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative, and stating the new location of the business Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
6. Valid ID of the representative (1 photocopy), if newly designated Applicant
7. Sketch / Google map of Business location (1 original) with pictures of the premise location Applicant
8. Tax Declaration of the Property or any proof of property ownership (owned, rented and not rented) and Lease Contract if rented or Consent from Property Owner if not rented Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
9. FSIC for Occupancy Permit valid in the last 9 months Bureau of Fire Protection
10. Affidavit of Undertaking that there had been no substantial changes made on the building Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public

Fees (printed page 78; PDF page 39): Step 1 application lists None. For Step 2 payment at the City Treasurer’s Office, the charter states: Mayor’s Permit Fee is based on the asset size and nature of business. Service fee is Php50.00. The PHP 50.00 service fee is not a quoted total inclusive of the variable Mayor’s Permit Fee.

old_reference: A Mayor's Business Permit in Davao City is valid for not more than one (1) year and expires on December 31 following issuance. Renewal must be filed within the month of January. Mandatory renewal requirements are: 1) List of Employees stating names and positions (1 copy); 2) Notarized Special Power of Attorney (Sole Proprietorship), Partnership Resolution, or Board Resolution/Secretary's Certificate (Corporation/Cooperative) if represented; 3) Valid ID of representative; 4) Valid Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) (1 photocopy); and 5) Specific clearances for regulated business lines.
new_reference:
Business permit validity and renewal (printed page 54; PDF page 15): The Business Permit is granted for a period of not more than one (1) year and shall expire on the thirty-first (31st) of December following the date of issuance unless revoked or surrendered earlier. The Business Permit issued shall be renewed within the month of January. It shall have a continuing validity only upon renewal thereof and payment of the corresponding fee.

The RENEWAL checklist (printed pages 55-56; PDF pages 16-17) lists the following seven rows. Each transcribed row includes its Where to Secure entry; preserve the conditions and document quantities as stated.

1. List of Employees stating the Name and Position of the Employees (1 copy) Applicant
2. For Sole Proprietorship, if represented, Special Power of Attorney, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. For Partnership, Partnership Resolution, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. For other form of ownership, Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate, indicating specific authority and capacity granted to representative. Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. Valid I.D. of the representative (1 photocopy), if newly designated Applicant
6. Valid Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (1 photocopy) Applicant or Bureau of Fire Protection
7. Specific requirements for specific line of business Concerned Agency

old_reference: An Occupational Permit is required for workers not holding a Professional Tax Receipt (PTR). It must be renewed annually on or before January 31; late renewal incurs a statutory 25% penalty. Fees are PHP 125.00 for new applications and timely renewals, and PHP 156.25 for late renewals. Requirements include: 1) Application form; 2) Certificate of Employment; 3) Official Receipt from CTO; 4) Notarized Affidavit of Consent for minors below 18 (or ages 18-20 for amusement places/bars); and 5) PSA Birth Certificate, Health ID, and interview for entertainers, masseurs, and bar attendants.
new_reference:
According to the Occupational Permit section of the thesis source charter (printed pages 104-106; PDF pages 65-67):

The charter states that an Occupational Permit is issued to any worker or employee who is not a holder of validly issued Professional Tax Receipts, whether working on a temporary or permanent basis.

Under Who may avail, it lists Filipino employees or workers aged 18 at application; foreigners may apply after securing an Alien Employment Permit from DOLE. Where the law allows a person below 18 to work, an Affidavit of Consent from the parent or guardian is required.

Renew annually on or before January 31. The charter states a 25% penalty for late renewal.

The fee table and TOTAL row state PHP 125.00 for new and updated renewal, and PHP 156.25 for late renewal. Payment is to the City Treasurer’s Office.

Application Form: Business Bureau Office, Window 1 or Public Assistance Desk. Certificate of Employment: applicant.

Checklist item 3 specifies Official Receipt (for service crew), from the City Treasurer’s Office. Separately, the process instructs walk-in applicants to submit required documents including the official receipt.

A notarized Affidavit of Consent is listed for minors below 18. For Night Clubs and related establishments and similar places of amusement, the affidavit is listed for ages 18 to 20.

Additional requirements for Entertainers, Masseurs, Bar Attendants: Birth Certificate (Philippine Statistics Authority); Valid ID of parent or qualified guardian for parent’s consent with appearance (Where to Secure: Any Notary public); Health ID (City Health).

The process note states: If the applicant is an entertainer, masseur, or bar attendant 18-20 years old, or the applicant is below 18 years old, he or she must present himself/herself for an interview. Agency action 2.2 repeats these conditions.

old_reference: For Full Retirement of a Business Permit upon cessation of operations, applicants must submit: 1) Latest original Business Permit or certified copy; 2) Notarized Affidavit of Full Retirement stating the reason and exact effective date of retirement (Single Proprietorship), or Partnership/Board Resolution; 3) Valid ID and SPA if represented; and 4) Physical surrender of the Business Identification Plate. Late filing fees range from PHP 1,000.00 to PHP 5,000.00 if the retirement application is submitted more than 30 days from actual business cessation, in addition to gross sales tax obligations assessed by the CTO.
new_reference:
For Full Retirement of Business Permit after business operations cease, the charter gives these client steps (printed pages 112-114; PDF pages 73-75):

1. Submit requirements for pre-assessment, receive and sign the retirement application, then proceed to the City Treasurer’s Office for assessment of dues and approval for retirement.
2. Submit the recommended approved retirement application and Business Identification Plate and receive a claim stub.
3. Receive the retired business permit and the applicant’s copies of required documents; the processing staff receives the claim stub and releases them.

Checklist (printed page 111; PDF page 72). Each transcribed row includes Where to Secure; retain its ownership and representation conditions:

1. Latest Business Permit (1 original or 1 certified copy) Applicant or Records Section, Business Bureau
2. Affidavit of Full Retirement indicating the reason and the effective date of retirement if Single Proprietorship. (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
3. Partnership Resolution duly signed by all the Partners stating the reason, effective date of retirement and the authorized representative indicated therein if Partnership. (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
4. Board Resolution or Secretary’s Certificate stating the reason and effective date of retirement, the authorized represented indicated therein if other forms of ownership (1 original) Applicant, notarized by any Notary Public
5. Valid I.D. of the authorized representative, if newly designated (1 photocopy) Applicant
6. Special Power of Attorney for Single Proprietorship if represented (1 original) Any Notary Public / Applicant
7. Business Identification Plate Applicant

The TOTAL fee cell states Tax Obligation based on gross sales, and a late filing fee of P1,000 to P5,000 for an application filed more than 30 days from cessation. The cell does not specify how to choose an amount within that range.

old_reference: Pursuant to Section 422 of the 2017 Revenue Code of Davao City (Ordinance No. 0291-17), all businesses must register their books of accounts, records of transactions, official receipts, cash sales invoices, and delivery receipts with the City Treasurer's Office within fifteen (15) working days from the date of filing the application for a new or renewal business permit. Failure to register within this 15-day period incurs a mandatory administrative fine of Five Thousand Pesos (PHP 5,000.00).
new_reference: The charter Annex 9 states that failure to register books of accounts, books of records, official receipts, cash sales, cash invoices, delivery receipts and other collection receipts within fifteen (15) working days from filing a new or renewal business-permit application incurs an administrative fine of PHP5,000.

old_reference: Under Section 34 of the 2017 Revenue Code of Davao City, the Tax on Transfer of Real Property Ownership is imposed at the rate of 0.75% (or up to 1%) based on the total consideration or the fair market value of the real property, whichever is higher. In addition, a Transfer Tax Certification fee of PHP 50.00 is charged (plus PHP 20.00 for every additional page). Requirements include the original notarized Deed of Transfer, photocopy of Title from the Registry of Deeds, and original Tax Declaration (DRPV).
new_reference:
The charter literally states: "Transfer Tax is equal to 87% or 1% based on the consideration or the market value whichever is higher." This reports the printed wording; the intended applicable rate is not resolved by that statement. Do not silently replace it with 0.75%.

The certification fee table lists PHP50 plus PHP20 for each additional page. Requirements: title photocopy for verification only; notarized Deed of Transfer (1 original); Tax Declaration/Declaration of Real Property Tax Valuation (1 original).

old_reference: Real Property Tax in Davao City consists of two statutory components under Ordinance No. 0291-17: 1) Section 7 imposes the Basic Real Property Tax as an annual ad valorem levy of one and one-half percent (1.5%) of the assessed value of real property (land, buildings, and machinery); and 2) Section 8 imposes an Additional Levy for the Special Education Fund (SEF) of one percent (1%) of the assessed value. The total annual levy is 2.5% of assessed property valuation.
new_reference: Annex11 states Basic Real Property Tax is 1.5% of assessed value and the additional Special Education Fund levy is 1% of assessed value. Their arithmetic sum is 2.5% of assessed value; this sum is derived from the two stated rates.

old_reference: Under Section 72 of Ordinance No. 0291-17, an annual fixed tax is imposed on delivery vehicles used by manufacturers, producers, wholesalers, dealers, or retailers distributing products within Davao City: a) Motorcycle and motorized tricycle: PHP 240.00; b) Delivery jeepney and utility vehicles: PHP 600.00; c) Trucks, vans, or vehicles with six wheels and above: PHP 1,000.00; d) Water vessels, barges, and tugboats: PHP 2,000.00; and e) Airplanes/aircraft: PHP 5,000.00.
new_reference: Annex15, Section72 lists annual fixed delivery-vehicle taxes: motorcycle/motorized tricycle PHP240; delivery jeepney/similar utility vehicle PHP600; truck, van, or any vehicle with six wheels and above PHP1,000; water vessel, barges, ferry boats, tugboats and similar watercraft PHP2,000; airplane/aircraft PHP5,000. The section applies to vehicles used by manufacturers, producers, wholesalers, dealers or retailers in delivery/distribution of the listed products and goods within the City. Preserve the six-wheel row wording when classifying a vehicle.

old_reference: Under Section 58 of the 2017 Revenue Code, the Professional Tax is PHP 300.00 per annum for individuals legally authorized to practice their profession. Applicants can register and generate an Order of Payment online via ptr.davaocity.gov.ph or pay at CTO counters. Requirements are: 1) Unexpired PRC ID or IBP ID (1 original); 2) Certification from PRC/IBP for new passers; and 3) Current Davao City address and contact details.
new_reference:
The Professional Tax service lists a TOTAL fee of PHP300. Requirements: unexpired PRC/IBP ID (1 original); PRC/IBP certification for new registrants/passers (1 original); current Davao City address and valid contact number/email address.

Register/log in at ptr.davaocity.gov.ph, generate an Order of Payment, then pay at a Miscellaneous Fees counter or the listed Landbank payment portal.

old_reference: Under Section 393 and 394 of Ordinance No. 0291-17, Community Tax (Cedula) is assessed as follows: For Individuals: Basic tax of PHP 5.00 plus an additional tax of PHP 1.00 for every PHP 1,000.00 of income derived from business, profession, or property, capped at a maximum of PHP 5,000.00. For Corporations: Basic annual tax of PHP 500.00 plus an additional tax of PHP 2.00 for every PHP 5,000.00 worth of real property owned in the Philippines and PHP 2.00 for every PHP 5,000.00 of gross receipts, capped at a maximum of PHP 10,000.00.
new_reference:
Annex14 states an annual basic community tax of PHP5 for liable individuals plus an annual additional tax of PHP1 per PHP1,000 of income, with the additional tax capped at PHP5,000. For husband and wife the additional tax is based on their total property and total gross receipts/earnings. The cap is on additional tax, not the basic-plus-additional total.

For liable corporations, the basic annual tax is PHP500 plus additional tax capped at PHP10,000. The additional schedule is PHP2 per PHP5,000 of Philippine real-property value during the preceding year using the stated real-property-tax valuation, plus PHP2 per PHP5,000 of Philippine business gross receipts/earnings during the preceding year. Intercorporate dividends are included in gross receipts/earnings for this additional tax. The cap is on additional tax.

old_reference: To secure a Building Permit under PD 1096, applicants must submit: 1) Notarized Application Letter; 2) Accomplished Unified Building Permit Form (5 copies); 3) Complete sets of Architectural, Civil/Structural, Sanitary/Plumbing, Electrical, and Mechanical Permit forms and plans (5 sets each), all duly signed and sealed by licensed professionals (Architect, Civil Engineer, Sanitary Engineer/Master Plumber, Professional Electrical Engineer, Professional Mechanical Engineer); 4) Certified true copies of Land Title (LRA), Tax Declaration, and Current Real Property Tax Receipt; 5) CPDO Zoning Locational Clearance; and 6) BFP Fire Safety Evaluation Clearance (FSEC).
new_reference:
The Building Permit checklist lists a notarized application letter; notarized Unified Building Permit Form with Civil/Architectural plans signed/sealed by a licensed Civil Engineer/Architect (5 accomplished form copies); Architectural, Civil/Structural, and Sanitary/Plumbing forms (3 form copies and 5 plan sets each). Civil/Structural plans identify a licensed Civil Engineer; Sanitary/Plumbing identifies a licensed Sanitary Engineer/Master Plumber. Architectural plans must be signed/sealed by the hired licensed professional.

Electrical: 3 accomplished form copies and 5 plan sets, signed/sealed by a Licensed Professional Electrical Engineer. Electronics: 2 form copies and 5 plan sets, signed/sealed by a Licensed Electronics Engineer. Mechanical row states "Mechanical Permit Form with 6-7 sets Mechanical Plans" signed and sealed by the hired professional "Licensed Electronics Engineer"; it separately lists "2 copies of accomplished Form" and "5 sets of plans". These are preserved as separate source statements. The user interprets the latter five sets as another submission; the row does not explicitly say additional or specify a combined total.

The checklist also lists Zoning Location Clearance and BFP Fire Safety Evaluation Certificate (1 original and 1 photocopy each); certified true copies of land title, property tax declaration and current real-property-tax receipt (1 original and 1 photocopy each); owner/applicant ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); PRC IDs, current PTR and TIN of signing professionals (1 photocopy per professional).

Other listed technical submissions include scaled sketch/lot and vicinity plans, relocation survey plans/reports signed/sealed by a licensed Geodetic Engineer (4 copies); technical specifications signed/sealed by a licensed Architect (2 copies); bill of materials/cost estimates signed/sealed by a licensed Architect (4 copies); seismic analysis; clear detailed location photographs with landmarks or Google Maps image.

Additional clearances are conditional: DPWH for structures along a National Highway; CAAP for tall structures; DENR ECC for environmentally critical projects; drainage clearance where stated; traffic impact assessment with site development/parking plans for major development; and RROW clearance for structures along City/Barangay/Subdivision roads. These rows list 1 original and 1 photocopy and preserve their stated conditions.

old_reference: For construction, addition, or minor repair of structures that are three (3) storeys and above, OCBO enforces mandatory conditional safety submittals: 1) Construction Safety & Health Program (CSHP) approved by the Department of Labor and Employment (DOLE) (1 original, 1 photocopy); and 2) Boring and Plate Load Soil Test Report (2 copies) signed and sealed by a licensed Civil/Geotechnical Engineer. If applying for an additional storey, an Affidavit manifesting that the existing foundation can support the proposed additional floors is required.
new_reference: Conditional requirements state: construction/minor repair of buildings 3 storeys and above requires Construction Safety & Health Program, 1 original and 1 photocopy, with DOLE listed under Where to Secure. Boring and Plate Load Test Result/Report is listed if the structure is at least three storeys, 2 copies, with a licensed Civil/Geotechnical Engineer listed. For an additional storey, submit an affidavit that the foundation can carry the proposed additional floors, 2 originals.

old_reference: Before any building can be used or occupied, an Occupancy Permit must be secured from OCBO. Documentary requirements are: 1) Application Letter; 2) Duly accomplished Certificate of Occupancy (1 original) and Certificate of Completion (1 original); 3) Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) from the BFP (1 original); 4) Project photographs showing four elevations (Front, Back, Left, Right); 5) Approved Building, Architectural, Structural, Sanitary, Electrical, and Mechanical Permits (1 photocopy); and 6) As-built plans if alterations were introduced.
new_reference:
Occupancy checklist: application letter (1 original); authorization letter if applicant is not owner (1 original); owner ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); Certificate of Occupancy (1 original); Certificate of Completion (1 original); BFP Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (1 original); four-elevation project pictures (front/back/left/right); approved Building Construction, Architectural, Civil/Structural, Sanitary/Plumbing, Electrical and Mechanical installation permits (1 photocopy); approved building-permit plan (1 original).

If a different professional undertook/was assigned the project, the checklist requires a signed, notarized waiver from the previous professional in charge (1 original). It also lists Structure Images with CAAP clearance and structural survey for actual building height, signed/sealed by a licensed Geodetic Engineer. The authorization-letter source cell says CPDO and the picture source cell says Hired Geodetic Engineer; those unusual source associations are preserved.

old_reference: While a main Building Permit is undergoing evaluation, the Building Official may issue a Ground Preparation and Excavation Permit (GP&EP) for foundation work, valid for thirty (30) days or until superseded by the building permit. Statutory fees are: 1) Inspection and Verification Fee of PHP 200.00; 2) Issuance fee of PHP 50.00; 3) Excavation fee of PHP 3.00 per cubic meter (or PHP 4.00 per cubic meter for foundations with basements); and 4) PHP 250.00 per square meter for authorized foundation encroachments into public areas.
new_reference: While the Building Permit is being processed, the Building Official may issue GP&EP for foundation subject to line-and-grade verification, inspection and review. It is valid only for 30 days or superseded upon Building Permit issuance. Fees: inspection/verification PHP200; excavation PHP3 per cubic meter; GP&EP issuance PHP50; foundation excavation with basement PHP4 per cubic meter; excavation other than foundation/basement PHP3 per cubic meter; permitted footing/foundation encroachment into public areas PHP250 per square meter or fraction thereof.

old_reference: A Fencing Permit is required prior to constructing a fence. Requirements include: 1) Fencing Permit form with 3 sets of Civil/Architectural plans signed and sealed by a licensed Civil Engineer/Architect; 2) Certified True Copy of Land Title (LRA/CASSO) and Tax Declaration; 3) Barangay Clearance; 4) Lot/Vicinity plan; and 5) Bill of Materials and Cost Estimates. The fee schedule under PD 1096 IRR is: PHP 3.00 per linear meter for fences made of masonry, metal, or concrete up to 1.80 meters in height; PHP 4.00 per linear meter for heights exceeding 1.80 meters; and PHP 2.40 per linear meter for fences made of indigenous materials, barbed, or hog wire.
new_reference:
Fencing checklist: permit form with 3 sets of Civil/Architectural plans signed/sealed by licensed Civil Engineer/Architect (A3 structural-plan option stated); certified land title and property tax declaration (1 original and 1 photocopy each); the next row repeats Certified True Copy of Tax Declaration of the Property with CTO as source; Barangay Clearance (1 original and 1 photocopy); scaled sketch/lot/vicinity plan signed/sealed by licensed Geodetic Engineer (3 sets); bill of materials/cost estimates signed/sealed by licensed Civil Engineer (3 sets); signing professionals PRC ID/current PTR (1 photocopy); owner/applicant ID with 3 specimen signatures (1 photocopy); conditional DPWH clearance along a National Highway.

For fencing made of masonry, metal or concrete: height <= 1.80 m costs PHP3.00 per linear meter; height > 1.80 m costs PHP4.00 per linear meter. Both printed source rows include "of fraction thereof". For indigenous materials, barbed, chicken or hog wire, the listed rate is PHP2.40 per linear meter. No additional height qualifier is stated in that row. The service introduction says not exceeding 1.80 m, while the fee table explicitly includes a higher-height rate; this candidate reproduces the fee table without resolving that scope discrepancy.

old_reference: To secure a Certified True Copy (CTC) of a Building Permit or related building documents from the OCBO Records Division, the applicant must submit: 1) Request Letter; 2) Photocopy of the Building Permit or reference details; 3) Photocopy of valid ID of owner with 3 specimen signatures; 4) Notarized SPA and processor's valid ID if represented; and 5) Original Affidavit of Loss if the original permit was lost. The statutory fee is PHP 50.00 per document (1 copy), paid at the City Treasurer's Office, with a standard turnaround time of 2 Days, 1 Hour, and 19 Minutes.
new_reference:
For a Certified True Copy, submit request letter; photocopy of Building Permit and other related documents; owner valid-ID photocopy with 3 signatures; if not owner, processor valid-ID photocopy with 3 signatures and original SPA; if lost, original Affidavit of Loss. The checklist does not offer reference details as a substitute for the photocopy.

Pay PHP50 per document (1 copy) at the City Treasurer’s Office. The printed TOTAL is 2 Days, 1 Hour, and 19 Minutes. Preserve this as the source-listed total, not an independently verified sum: listed steps include two separate 3-hour entries plus 2 days and other minutes.

old_reference: Under the Integrated Zoning Ordinance (2019–2028), CPDO executes mandatory Validation of Occupancy Permits for structures that are 3-storeys and above OR possess a building floor area of 1,500 square meters and above. Requirements are: 1) Approved Building Plans (1 original); 2) Approved Building Permit from OBO (1 original); 3) Certificate of Occupancy Form (1 original); 4) Locational Clearance photocopy; and 5) Actual pictures of the building (1 original). The filing fee is PHP 150.00, and processing time is 3 Days, 2 Hours, and 10 Minutes.
new_reference:
The source describes validation for "3-storey buildings and above and for building floor area of 1,500 square meters and above only." User clarification: either category can qualify (3-storey and above OR floor area of 1,500 square meters and above). This alternative-trigger interpretation is user-supplied; the cited PDF itself uses "and" and does not independently resolve that interpretation.

Checklist: approved building plans (1 original); approved building permit (1 original); Certificate of Occupancy Form (1 original); Locational Clearance, if applicable (1 photocopy); pictures of building (1 original); Order of Payment (1 original); Official Receipt (1 original).

Filing fee is PHP150.00. The stated TOTAL is 3 Days, 2 Hours, and 10 Minutes; the final-approval step depends on availability of the Zoning Administrator.

old_reference: To obtain a Locational Clearance (LC) for Building Permit for structures 2-storeys and below, applicants must submit: 7 complete sets of signed/sealed building plans, certified true copy of title, accomplished building permit form, sketch plan with vicinity map, bill of materials, and notarized deed of sale or contract of lease. Fees consist of: 1) GIS Map Plotting fee of PHP 300.00; 2) Filing fee of PHP 150.00 for agricultural/residential, or PHP 300.00 for commercial/industrial; and 3) Zoning fee equivalent to 1/10 of 1% of the total building cost. Processing turnaround is 4 Days, 2 Hours, and 25 Minutes.
new_reference:
For Locational Clearance for Building Permit for 2-storey and below, the zoning fee is 1/10 of 1% of building cost for agricultural/residential and commercial/industrial/institutional categories. Filing fees are PHP150 per application for agricultural/residential and PHP300 per application for commercial/industrial.

The Map Plotting step separately lists a PHP300 filing fee, with order of payment issued by OBO. The TOTAL row lists 4 Days, 2 Hours, and 25 Minutes. The source does not explicitly list an institutional filing fee or explain aggregation of the map-plotting charge in the TOTAL row.

old_reference: If a Locational Clearance is denied by the Zoning Administrator, an applicant may file a Motion for Reconsideration before the Local Zoning Board of Adjustment and Appeals (LZBAA). Requirements are: 1) Letter of Reconsideration; 2) Denial Letter; 3) Title/Lease Contract; 4) Site sketch plan with vicinity landmarks; 5) Barangay Council Resolution of No Objection; 6) Locational mapping of neighbor's consent signatories; and 7) Notarized Affidavit of Non-Objection from adjoining property owners. The processing fee is PHP 600.00, and evaluation involves TWG site inspection, committee deliberation, and LZBAA board resolution.
new_reference:
Motion for Reconsideration is an appeal against denial of Locational Clearance by the Zoning Administrator. The checklist lists: Letter of Reconsideration; Denial Letter; Order of Payment; Official Receipt; Business Permit Application Form/Building Permit Application Form (for building permit); certified true copy of title(s)/Contract of Lease/Deed of Sale; site sketch with vicinity map and landmarks; Barangay Council Resolution Interposing No Objection; affidavit of non-objection of adjoining property owners; locational mapping of neighbor consent signatories; Affidavit of Undertaking; and Building Permit for a business-permit application.

Secure checklist and pre-evaluation; once documents are complete, obtain the order for the PHP600 processing fee. Submit original and photocopied official receipt with one complete set of documents. The process includes TWG site inspection/evaluation, TWG meeting with the applicant, committee deliberation, and, if approved, resolution and endorsement to OBO or Business Bureau. Claim the endorsement with attached resolution. Non-approved/deferred cases may receive NOC, NOD or disapproval.

old_reference: Under CPDO Service 12, Locational Clearance for Business (Online Application via appbts.davaocity.gov.ph) evaluates land-use compatibility under the Integrated ZO 2019-2028. Requirements uploaded to the portal are: 1) Filled-up application form; 2) Affidavit of Undertaking for neighbor's consent with sketch map; 3) Homeowners Association Certificate of No Objection (if inside a subdivision); 4) Proof of business working area pictures and road access; and 5) Certificate of Actual Land Occupancy (if inside ancestral land under RA 8371). There are no direct filing fees (None), and approval or issuance of a denial letter takes 1 Day and 50 Minutes.
new_reference:
For online business locational clearance, the checklist lists: uploaded application form; Affidavit of Undertaking for neighbor consent with sketch map showing neighbor location (1 photocopy); Homeowners Association Certificate of No Objection; Certificate of Actual Land Occupancy for Migrant (based on RA8371); Locational Clearance for Building Permit, if applicable; PRC ID for licensed broker/License to Sell/Affidavit of Undertaking not to sell raw lots (PD957); Affidavit of Undertaking for Online Business/Booking Office/On-Job Site/On-Call/Private Garage; pictures showing working area including roads; and sketch map. Additional requirements may be required as the need arises.

The fee columns and TOTAL state None. The TOTAL is 1 Day and 50 Minutes. This includes denial-letter steps, with signature time dependent on administrator availability; it is not a guaranteed approval deadline. Approved/conditionally approved cases have their BPLS status updated and other offices then evaluate the application.

old_reference: A Certificate of Compatibility is issued by the CPDO Zoning Enforcement Division to certify that proposed land activities are capable of co-existing harmoniously with adjacent zoning classifications. Requirements include: 1) Application Letter; 2) Zoning Certificate from CPDO; and 3) CTO Official Receipt. The filing fee is PHP 300.00, and the total administrative processing time is 1 Hour and 20 Minutes.
new_reference:
The Certificate of Compatibility certifies uses or land activities capable of existing together harmoniously. Checklist: Application Letter, Zoning Certificate from CPDO, and Official Receipt from CTO.

Filing fee is PHP300. The stated TOTAL is 1 Hour and 20 Minutes. The initial/final signature step is 15 minutes depending on availability of the Acting Zoning Administrator.

old_reference: Under the BFP Citizen's Charter and RA 9514, the Fire Safety Inspection Certificate (FSIC) for Occupancy Permit requires: 1) Endorsement from the Office of the Building Official (OBO); 2) Certificate of Completion; 3) As-built plans (if changes occurred); 4) Certified true copy of the assessment fee from OBO; and 5) Fire insurance policy (if any). The Fire Safety Inspection Fee (FSIF) is assessed at 15% of all regulatory fees charged by the LGU, but in no case shall the fee be lower than Five Hundred Pesos (PHP 500.00).
new_reference: For FSIC for Certificate of Occupancy and new/renewal business applications, the fee panel states FSIF is 15% of all fees charged by LGU/PEZA, not less than PHP500. It explicitly adds: if assessment from LGUs/PEZA is zero, FSIF is zero. Other fees apply if applicable under the cited RIRR provision. Do not omit the zero-assessment exception or narrow the base to LGU-only regulatory fees.

old_reference: Under the BFP Citizen's Charter and Joint Memorandum Circular (JMC) No. 2021-01, frontline transactions in Fire Stations, OSCP, and eBOSS are classified into three strict processing times: 1) Simple Transactions are processed within One (1) working day; 2) Complex Transactions are processed within Three (3) working days; and 3) Highly Technical Transactions are processed within Seven (7) working days.
new_reference: The BFP charter classifies Simple transactions as processed within 1 day, Complex within 3 days, and Highly Technical within 7 days. It directs readers to JMC2021-01 for classification coverage. The source says days, not working days, and identifies FIRE STATION/OSCP/BOSS.

old_reference: Under BFP Memorandum Circular No. 2016-016 and public anti-corruption warnings, the Bureau of Fire Protection does not accredit, endorse, or recommend any specific brand, store, or distributor of fire extinguishers or fire fighting equipment. BFP personnel are strictly prohibited from selling or recommending fire extinguishers. Portable fire extinguishers are regulated by the Department of Trade and Industry (DTI) through the Bureau of Product Standards (BPS), and establishments may purchase any brand that complies with Philippine National Standards (PNS).
new_reference:
The BFP public warning says it does not accredit or recommend any brand, store or distributor of fire extinguishers/fire-fighting equipment. Its warning prohibits personnel from selling or recommending a specific fire-extinguisher brand.

The image panel says portable fire extinguishers are regulated by DTI through BPS and that each type must comply with appropriate Philippine National Standards for product safety/reliability. This supports no BFP brand accreditation; it should not be expanded into a claim that any product is suitable regardless of type or hazard.
